engine: markdown
title: "Bioinformatics (FASTA/FASTQ)"
---

Sequence files (`.fasta`, `.fa`, `.fna`, `.fastq`, `.fq`) are read and written
with [microseq](https://github.com/larssnip/microseq). FASTA files produce a
data frame with `Header` and `Sequence` columns; FASTQ adds a `Quality` column.

## FASTA

### Reading

```{term}
rush run -n 'head(df)' sequences.fasta
```

### Writing

```{term}
rush run -n -O fasta -o output.fasta 'df' data.csv
```

## FASTQ

### Reading

```{term}
rush run -n 'head(df)' reads.fastq
```

### Writing

```{term}
rush run -n -O fastq -o output.fastq 'df' data.csv
```

## Example workflows

```bash
rush run 'nrow(df)' sequences.fasta
rush run 'df |> dplyr::filter(nchar(Sequence) > 100)' reads.fastq
rush convert -o filtered.fasta data.csv
```
